meta.description: Download large datasets from NCBI efficiently using EPost, history server, batching, rate limiting, and retry logic. Use when bulk-fetching tens of thousands of sequences, pulling all results of a large ESearch, designing reproducible pipelines, comparing E-utilities to NCBI Datasets v2 CLI, or implementing checksum-validated downloads. Encodes WebEnv TTL (~8h), EPost 200-ID limit, retmax caps, parallelization design, and integrity verification.

scientific_integrity.detail: All data in every executed input is real, live NCBI content (real accessions, real PMIDs, real record counts). No fabricated DOI/PMID/statistic anywhere in the Skill's text or in any executed output.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure data-retrieval-engineering skill; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-facing content anywhere in scope.

methodological_ground.detail: Retrieval-strategy selection (EFetch vs EPost vs history-server vs Datasets CLI), rate-limit math, and ToS/off-hours guidance are all methodologically sound and, where checked, independently confirmed accurate against live NCBI (200-ID EPost limit, 9,999-record silent retmax cap, exact shape of the expired-WebEnv HTTP-200 error body).

code_usability.detail: Two of the Skill's three shipped example scripts crash with an unhandled exception on realistic, documented invocations, both independently reproduced live (not by inspection): (1) examples/batch_fasta.py's own worked query (Homo sapiens insulin[Gene Name]) returns Count=0 on live NCBI, and history_server_download() correctly returns early without creating the output file, but the unconditional SeqIO.parse('insulin_mrna.fasta', ...) immediately below crashes with FileNotFoundError -- confirmed independently twice (the 2026-09-17 tooling pass and this audit's own rerun, run/support_verify_batch_fasta_crash.py). (2) examples/robust_download.py's checkpointed_download(), the Skill's 'production-grade' example built specifically to demonstrate WebEnv-expiry recovery, raises TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str' on the exact documented expired-session response (HTTP 200 with an <ERROR> body) -- live-confirmed in this audit's Input 5 by forging an invalid WebEnv/QueryKey pair and observing NCBI's real response shape first (run/support_check_bad_webenv.py), then running the shipped, unmodified checkpointed_download() against it (run/input5_robust_expiry.py). SKILL.md's own inline reference implementation of the same pattern has the missing bytes-decode guard the shipped example lacks. This matches the standard this audit lineage applied to the comparable pre-fix, unmodified-upstream state of entrez-fetch (3 confirmed unhandled-exception bugs on documented code patterns -> FAIL).

functional_suitability.note: Decision matrix, rate-limit math, EPost specifics, and batch-size guidance are complete and (where checked) correct; Correctness docked because 2 of 3 shipped examples crash on their own worked cases (see Reliability / Research Veto).

reliability.note: SKILL.md's own inline checkpoint/retry/WebEnv-refresh pattern is genuinely robust (verified live through a simulated crash, Input 2), but the flagship 'production-grade' example (robust_download.py) crashes with a raw, undiagnosed TypeError on exactly the failure mode it exists to demonstrate, and batch_fasta.py crashes with a raw FileNotFoundError on its own default query.

performance_context.note: Reasonable length, table-driven, no unnecessary repetition; usage-guide.md separates prompts from reference material.

agent_usability.note: Strong, consistent terminology and a genuinely useful decision matrix / failure-modes / common-errors table set; feedback design is good but not perfect (some code patterns print progress, others don't).

human_usability.note: usage-guide.md's Example Prompts read naturally, but Forgiveness is low: the two broken examples fail with raw stack traces on an entirely foreseeable real-world case (a query that returns 0 results today), not a clean, documented stop.

security.note: No hardcoded real secrets (API key is a documented 'YOUR_KEY' placeholder, consistent with the sibling Entrez skills in this folder); query strings go into GET params only, no code execution of user input.

maintainability.note: Decent modularity across 3 example files plus SKILL.md/usage-guide.md; Testability docked because the Skill's own verify_fasta_count()/integrity-check idea is sound but not actually applied defensively inside 2 of its 3 own examples.

agent_specific.note: Excellent Related-Skills composability and correct, verified idempotency (checkpoint/resume). Escape Hatches is the one real gap: strong hard caps for worker concurrency but only a soft 'consider' for record counts far beyond the documented brackets (see Input 7).

key_strengths: Core EPost + history-server + WebEnv/QueryKey batching pattern (SKILL.md's own inline code and examples/batch_by_ids.py) is fully correct: verified live across 4 independent tests (600-ID EPost/fetch, 368-record checkpoint+resume through a simulated crash, exact 200/201 EPost boundary enforcement, and an 8,768-record PubMed MEDLINE bulk pull) with zero record loss or duplication in every case.

Documented numeric constraints are accurate and independently verified against live NCBI: the 200-ID EPost hard limit, the legacy-ESearch 9,999-record silent retmax cap, and the exact HTTP-200-with-<ERROR>-body shape of an expired/invalid WebEnv session.

Checkpoint/resume design (SKILL.md's checkpointed_batch_download) survives a simulated mid-job crash cleanly: correct resume point, no duplicate or missing records, checkpoint file removed only on true completion.

Decision-matrix and rate-limit/ToS guidance (when to defect to Datasets CLI, worker-concurrency cap, off-hours scheduling) produced correct agent guidance under both a scope-boundary and an adversarial test.

recommendations.title: batch_fasta.py crashes on its own worked example (0-count query, no file guard)
recommendations.problem: Running examples/batch_fasta.py as shipped raises an unhandled FileNotFoundError. history_server_download() correctly detects a live Count=0 for its own worked query and returns early without creating 'insulin_mrna.fasta', but the module-level code immediately below unconditionally calls SeqIO.parse('insulin_mrna.fasta', 'fasta'), which crashes because the file was never created. Independently confirmed twice: the 2026-09-17 tooling pass and this audit's own rerun (run/support_verify_batch_fasta_crash.py).
recommendations.root_cause: The integrity-check block has no guard for the 0-count case the function itself already detects and returns for; separately, the shipped query ('insulin[Gene Name]') is stale -- NCBI's [Gene Name] field requires the official gene symbol, not a descriptive English word, and has returned Count=0 on every date checked in this audit lineage.
recommendations.fix: Guard the integrity-check block, e.g. 'if elapsed == 0: print("No records found -- nothing to verify") else: records = list(SeqIO.parse(...))'. Replace the query with one verified to return a non-trivial live count, e.g. 'Homo sapiens[ORGN] AND INS[GENE] AND srcdb_refseq[PROP] AND biomol_mrna[PROP]' or the already-verified 'BRCA1[GENE] AND Homo sapiens[ORGN] AND biomol_mrna[PROP] AND srcdb_refseq[PROP]' (368 hits, confirmed live 2026-09-19).

recommendations.title: robust_download.py crashes with TypeError on the exact WebEnv-expiry scenario it exists to demonstrate
recommendations.problem: checkpointed_download()'s error-body check ('<ERROR>' in body[:500]) assumes body is str, but Entrez.efetch(...).read() returns bytes on the currently-installed Biopython 1.88/urllib stack. Live-confirmed in Input 5: forcing the documented expired-session response (HTTP 200 with an XML <ERROR> body, independently reproduced against a forged WebEnv/QueryKey) raises TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str' before the intended recovery branch ever runs -- defeating the entire purpose of this 'production-grade' example.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's own reference implementation of the identical pattern (checkpointed_batch_download) already has the guard 'if isinstance(body, bytes): body = body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")' immediately after h.read(); this line was dropped when robust_download.py was written as a separate, expanded copy.
recommendations.fix: Add the identical isinstance(body, bytes) decode guard to robust_download.py, in the same place SKILL.md's own inline pattern has it. Also replace the script's stale worked-example query (mouse 'hemoglobin[Gene Name]', Count=0 live) with a verified-nonzero one, matching the P0-1 fix.

recommendations.title: No hard stop-condition for requests far outside E-utilities' efficient range
recommendations.problem: For a request to bulk-download the entire nucleotide database (500M+ sequences) via EFetch, the decision matrix only offers a soft '>100,000 sequences: Consider FTP mirror or Datasets CLI; chunk if E-utils still [used]' -- there is no instruction to refuse or hard-redirect at extreme scale, unlike the explicit, quantified hard cap given for worker concurrency ('Never exceed 4 concurrent workers... or 1 without').
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's Agent-Specific escape-hatch guidance is strong for the parallelism anti-pattern but was never extended to the scale dimension, leaving a literal-minded agent able to be talked into a technically-compliant but multi-week single-stream E-utilities loop for a request this Skill's own tools were never designed to serve.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit escape hatch to the decision matrix: for record counts far beyond the documented >100,000 bracket (e.g. >1,000,000, or a literal 'entire database' request), instruct the agent to refuse the EFetch-loop approach outright and point only to NCBI's full bulk FTP/BLAST-db mirrors or Datasets CLI, the same way the Failure Modes section already hard-warns against parallelism.

recommendations.title: [Gene Name]/[GENE] field-tag precision is undocumented, and caused both broken example queries
recommendations.problem: Neither SKILL.md nor usage-guide.md warns that NCBI's [Gene Name]/[GENE] search field requires the official gene symbol, not a descriptive English word -- the exact gap that made both batch_fasta.py's (insulin[Gene Name]) and robust_download.py's (hemoglobin[Gene Name]) shipped queries return Count=0 on live NCBI.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill documents rate limits, WebEnv lifecycle, and batching precisely, but has no equivalent precision note for query-term construction, an easy blind spot to reproduce when writing new example queries.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note near the Decision Matrix: 'Gene-related field tags ([GENE], [Gene Name]) require the database's official gene symbol (verify via ESearch or the entrez-search skill's EInfo pattern), not a descriptive term.'
